tags.chapter_name: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

question.text: $5.75 \mathrm{mg}$ of sodium vapour is converted to sodium ion. If the ionisation energy of sodium is $490 \mathrm{~kJ} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}$ and atomic weight is 23 units, the amount of energy needed for this conversion will be

solution.text:
$\mathrm{Na}(\mathrm{g}) \longrightarrow \mathrm{Na}^{+}(\mathrm{g})+\mathrm{e}^{-}$
$1 \mathrm{~mol} \mathrm{Na}(\mathrm{g})$
requires $490 \mathrm{~kJ} /$ mol for ionization.
$\therefore \quad \frac{5.75 \times 10^{-3}}{23}$ mol $\quad$ requires $490 \mathrm{~kJ} \times \frac{5.75 \times 10^{-3}}{23}=0.1225 \mathrm{~kJ}=122.5 \mathrm{~J}$
